readings.heading: Ὁ Ἀπόστολος τοῦ Μάρτυρος — 1 Peter 1:1–25, 2:1–10
verses: 1. Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, to God's chosen people, strangers scattered through Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia —
2. chosen, as God the Father knew beforehand, made holy by the Spirit, so that you might obey Jesus Christ and be sprinkled with his blood. Grace to you, and peace, in full measure.
3. Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ. In his great mercy he has given us a new birth into a living hope, through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead —
4. into an inheritance that can never spoil or stain or fade, kept in the heavens for you.
5. God's own power is guarding you through your faith, for a salvation that is ready to be revealed at the last time.
6. This is what you rejoice in, even if now, for a little while, you have had to suffer grief in all kinds of trials.

7. They come so that your faith, tested and proved genuine — far more precious than gold, which perishes even though fire tests it — may be found worthy of praise and honour and glory on the day when Jesus Christ is revealed.
8. You have never seen him, and you love him. You cannot see him now, yet you believe in him — and you rejoice with a joy beyond words, full of glory,
9. because you are receiving the goal of your faith: the salvation of your souls.
10. The prophets searched and enquired about this salvation — the prophets who foretold the grace that was coming to you.
11. They asked who and when the Spirit of Christ in them was pointing to, when it testified beforehand to the sufferings Christ would go through, and to the glories that would follow.

12. It was revealed to them that they were serving not themselves but you, in all the things that have now been announced to you by those who brought you the gospel, through the Holy Spirit sent from heaven — things that even the angels long to look into.
13. So pull yourselves together; keep a clear head; set your hope completely on the grace that is being brought to you when Jesus Christ is revealed.
14. Like obedient children, do not go on shaping yourselves by the desires you had before, in the days when you did not know any better.
15. The One who called you is holy — so be holy yourselves in everything you do,
16. because it is written: "You shall be holy, for I am holy."
17. And since you call him Father — the One who judges each person's work without favourites — live out the time of your stay here in reverent fear,
18. knowing what it cost to set you free from the empty way of life your fathers handed down to you. It was not something perishable, silver or gold,
19. but the precious blood of Christ, like that of a lamb without blemish and without spot.
20. He was marked out before the world was founded, and revealed in these last times for your sake.
21. Through him you believe in God, who raised him from the dead and gave him glory — and so your faith and your hope rest on God.
22. You have purified your souls by obeying the truth through the Spirit, for a genuine love of the brothers and sisters. So love one another deeply, from a pure heart.
23. You have been born again — not from a seed that perishes, but from one that does not: through the living word of God, which lasts for ever.
24. Because: "All flesh is like grass, and all human glory like the flower of grass. The grass withers, and its flower falls,
25. but the word of the Lord remains for ever." And that word is the good news that was preached to you.
2.1. So put away all malice, all deceit, all hypocrisy and envy, and every kind of slander,
2. and like newborn babies, long for the pure milk of the word, so that by it you may grow,
3. since you have tasted that the Lord is good.
4. Come to him, the living stone — rejected by human beings, but chosen and precious in God's sight —
5. and you too, like living stones, are being built into a spiritual house, a holy priesthood, to offer spiritual sacrifices that God accepts, through Jesus Christ.
6. Because Scripture says: "See, I am laying in Sion a cornerstone, chosen and precious; and whoever believes in him will not be put to shame."
7. So the honour is yours, you who believe. But for those who disobey: "The stone the builders rejected has become the head of the corner,"
8. and "a stone to stumble over, a rock to trip on." They stumble because they disobey the word — and that is what they were appointed for.

9. But you are a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people God has claimed for his own, so that you may proclaim the mighty deeds of the One who called you out of darkness into his wonderful light —
10. you who once were no people at all, but now are God's people; who had received no mercy, but now have received mercy.

readings.heading: Ὁ Ἀπόστολος τῆς ἡμέρας — 1 Corinthians 16:4–12
verses: 4. Brothers and sisters: and if it is fitting for me to go as well, they will travel with me.
5. I will come to you when I have passed through Macedonia — for I am only passing through Macedonia.
6. But with you I may stay a while, or even spend the winter, so that you can send me on my way wherever I go.
7. I do not want to see you now just in passing; I hope to stay with you for some time, if the Lord permits.
8. I will stay on in Ephesus until Pentecost,
9. for a great and effective door has opened to me — and there are many opponents.
10. If Timothy comes, see that he is among you without fear, for he is doing the work of the Lord, as I am.
11. So let no one look down on him. Send him on his way in peace, so that he may come to me — I am expecting him with the brothers.
12. As for our brother Apollos: I urged him strongly to come to you with the brothers, but it was not at all his will to come now. He will come when he has the opportunity.

readings.heading: Τὸ Εὐαγγέλιον — Matthew 21:28–32
verses: 28. At that time Jesus said: "What do you think? A man had two sons. He went to the first and said, 'Son, go and work in my vineyard today.'
29. He answered, 'I will not' — but afterwards he changed his mind and went.
30. And he went to the second and said the same. He answered, 'I will, sir' — and did not go.

31. Which of the two did the father's will?" They said to him, "The first." Jesus said to them: "I tell you the truth: the tax collectors and the prostitutes are going into the kingdom of God ahead of you.

32. For John came to you in the way of righteousness, and you did not believe him; but the tax collectors and the prostitutes believed him. And you, even when you saw it, did not change your minds afterwards and believe him."
